claim_as_stated: O*NET current database release 31.0; RDF format availability; O*NET AI-impact methods report (June 2026)
correct_statement: O*NET 31.0 released August 2026 (218 occupations updated). In July 2026 O*NET added CSV, JSON and RDF downloads; 31.0 is published in Turtle, N-Triples and RDF/XML. The June 2026 report is 'Indexing the Impact of AI within the O*NET System: A Review of Methods and Development of Recommendations'. Site updated Oct 6, 2026. No release after 31.0 is announced on What's New.
note: The 'next update Nov 2026' in ST-18 was not confirmed. The Work Context modernization report is dated August 2026 on the reports list and September 2026 on What's New.

claim_as_stated: SOC 2028 revision status (Federal Register notices); second notice TBD
correct_statement: The first FRN was published June 12, 2024 (docket BLS-2024-0001-0001; comments closed Aug 12, 2024). The SOCPC is still reviewing input. The second FRN (initial recommendations) is 'TBD'. The third FRN (final 2028 SOC) is planned for 2027, for use from reference year 2028. Page last modified Sep 30, 2026.
source_publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics / SOC Policy Committee

claim_as_stated: Workforce Pell live Jul 1, 2026 with state boards approving programs; WIOA reauthorization (A Stronger Workforce for America Act, H.R. 8210, 2026) status
correct_statement: Workforce Pell: ED released the final rule May 18, 2026, and students can use Pell for eligible short programs from July 1, 2026. Programs run 150-599 clock hours over 8 to under 15 weeks. Governors, working with state workforce boards, identify in-demand occupations and approve programs; ED then reviews and the Secretary approves. So 'state boards approving' should read 'governors (with state workforce boards) approving'. H.R. 8210 was introduced Apr 6, 2026 and ordered reported, amended, 19-14 by House Education and Workforce on Apr 21, 2026. No House floor vote or Senate action was found. WIOA is still not reauthorized.
source_title: ED Releases Final Rule on Workforce Pell; H.R. 8210 bill detail
note: The correction is minor: who approves programs. The Federal Register citation and effective date of the final rule were not retrieved; the ACTE post links to a public-inspection document.

claim_as_stated: CESU Network: 17.5% indirect cost cap; number of partners (500+); NRCS 10%
correct_statement: There are 17 CESUs and more than 500 partners. Work under CESU master agreements is limited to a 17.5% network overhead (F&A) rate.
source_title: CESU Fact Sheet (DoD) / UF Research: Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Units
source_publisher: DoD Legacy (DENIX); University of Florida Division of Sponsored Programs
note: The NRCS 10% exception was not confirmed by either source, so treat it as unverified. The 500+ partner count dates from April 2024.

claim_as_stated: The Corps Network: ~140 corps, 22,000+ participants/year; Resource Assistants Program with USFS
correct_statement: TCN represents 140 member organizations that engage more than 22,000 young people a year. The Resource Assistants Program is a paid immersive internship with the U.S. Forest Service. It requires 960+ hours and an associate degree or two-year certificate, and leads to up to two years of noncompetitive hiring eligibility.
note: The page does not show RAP was active in 2025-26 or how many RAs there are. Check this before claiming current RAP scale, given the USFS hiring freezes (see V1-04).

claim_as_stated: Credential issuers: REHS/RS (NEHA), CHMM (IHMM), CFM (ASFPM), CPESC (EnviroCert), PWS (SWS PCP), CWB (TWS), SAF Certified Forester, CERP (SER), ISA Certified Arborist, QEP (IPEP), ISSP-CSP, LEED AP (USGBC), state water/wastewater operator certification (ABC)
correct_statement: Confirmed: REHS/RS by NEHA; CHMM by IHMM (active, May 2026 newsletter); CFM by ASFPM (since 1999); CPESC by EnviroCert International (JTA v1.1, May 2024); PWS by the SWS Professional Certification Program (wetlandcert.org); CWB/AWB by TWS (2026 Certification Program Manual); Certified Forester by SAF; CERP/CERPIT by SER (new CERPs Apr 2025); ISA Certified Arborist by ISA; QEP/EPI by IPEP (identity confirmed, no 2025-26 activity source found). Corrections: ISSP-SA/ISSP-CSP are offered by GBCI (since Dec 2019), not ISSP alone. The LEED AP credential is administered by GBCI (since 2008), with LEED itself owned by USGBC. Water and wastewater operator certification is issued by state programs under SDWA s.1419 guidelines; ABC supplies standardized exams and need-to-know criteria that many states use (e.g., TN, MT). ABC is not the issuer.

source_publisher: NEHA; IHMM; ASFPM; EnviroCert; SWS PCP; TWS; SAF/O*NET; SER; ISA; IPEP/A&WMA; BD+C; I+S; TN TDEC / MT DEQ
note: Update credentials_register.csv: DB-CR-057 issuer to GBCI (LEED by USGBC); DB-CR-060 issuer to GBCI (developed by ISSP); operator-cert rows to issuer = state, exam = ABC. Renewal cycles were not checked.

claim_as_stated: NCES CIP 2020 and the CIP-SOC crosswalk (current version / any 2025-26 update)
correct_statement: CIP 2020 is the current edition. The official crosswalk is CIP 2020 to SOC 2018 (Excel, with 2020 Guidelines for Using the CIP to SOC Crosswalk). The NCES resources page shows no 2025-26 update or CIP 2030 announcement.
note: The crosswalk will need a re-map when SOC 2028 is final (2027).

claim_as_stated: Status of major funders' environmental-workforce/AI programs (Moore, Packard, Walton, Doris Duke, Bezos Earth Fund AI for Climate & Nature Grand Challenge, Google.org AI Collaborative: Wildfires, Schmidt Sciences)
correct_statement: Bezos Earth Fund AI for Climate and Nature Grand Challenge: Phase II awards announced Oct 23, 2025, giving 15 teams up to $2M each ($30M total), with no next round announced. Google.org AI Collaborative: Wildfires launched Mar 17, 2025 with more than $27M and 15+ organizations (incl. Moore Foundation and Earth Fire Alliance), and was still making grants in Jul 2026 (UCSD SCIL). Moore Foundation: Wildfire Resilience Initiative, $110M over six years (Feb 2023). Walton Family Foundation: Environment Program active, with a new director named Feb 2026. Doris Duke Foundation: Environment program active (climate-smart forests, Indigenous-led conservation). Schmidt Sciences: AI in Science postdoctoral fellowships still being advertised for 2026. None of these funders runs a program dedicated to environmental workforce skills; their AI programs are about tools and solutions.
source_title: Bezos Earth Fund Announces $30 Million in AI Grand Challenge Awards; New AI Collaboratives to take action on wildfires and food insecurity; Moore Foundation commits $110 million for wildfire resilience
source_publisher: Bezos Earth Fund; Google (blog.google); Chronicle of Philanthropy; Walton Family Foundation; Doris Duke Foundation
note: Packard was not checked (budget). The Schmidt Sciences evidence is indirect (fellowship job ads). The Doris Duke Charitable Foundation is now named the Doris Duke Foundation.

claim_as_stated: Is there an existing environment-sector-wide coalition focused on workforce skills and AI (e.g., Coalition of Natural Resource Societies)?
correct_statement: No standing coalition focused on workforce skills and AI was found. The 'Coalition of Natural Resource Societies' could not be confirmed as an active body: a direct search returned nothing. The closest current activity is ad hoc joint statements, e.g., AFS, SAF, SRM and TWS on federal workforce reductions (Feb 27, 2025). That statement names no standing coalition and does not mention AI or skills frameworks.
source_title: Natural resource professional societies issue joint statement on the impacts of federal workforce reduction
note: On this evidence EMST's convening role looks open. Present the four-society joint-statement group as a partner prospect, not as an existing coalition.

correct_statement: FY2026 round: EPA estimated $10-14M with up to $500,000 per grant over up to five years, and applications were due Sep 26, 2025. Selections were published Jan 27, 2026 (page updated Aug 10, 2026): about $12M to 25 communities.

claim_as_stated: NWCG and USWFS aligned wildland fire qualifications effective Jan 2027
correct_statement: The 2026 IQCS Transition Plan (Jan 28, 2026), which implements DOI SO 3443 and USFS SM 1078-017, says 'USWFS and USFS aligned qualification standards will be effective January 2027'. The alignment is between USWFS and USFS federal standards (the Federal Wildland Fire Qualifications Supplement), not NWCG. Existing qualifications carry over, and some positions will be archived. Separately, NWCG updated PMS 310-1 on Jan 23, 2026, changing position names and CIM/IPTM requirements.
source_title: 2026 Transition Plan; 2026 Updates to the NWCG Standards for Wildland Fire Position Qualifications, PMS 310-1
note: Say 'USWFS-USFS aligned federal qualification standards (Jan 2027)', not 'NWCG and USWFS'. A draft 2027 guide was expected in spring 2026 and was not checked.
